compound_ladder.label: calibrated (0.21% of lap time)
compound_ladder.derivation: fresh-tyre step prior 0.171 s (calibrated (0.21% of lap time)). The races identify the *net* cost of one step harder over a whole stint, holding stint length and race phase fixed: Melbourne 2024 -0.459 +/- 0.240 s; japan-2026 -0.069 +/- 0.664 s; barcelona-2026 +0.060 +/- 0.336 s; austria-2026 +0.106 +/- 0.295 s; belgium-2026 +0.075 +/- 0.323 s; hungary-2026 -0.010 +/- 0.327 s; italy-2026 +0.173 +/- 0.354 s -> pooled -0.066 +/- 0.122 s per step. The model's fresh-tyre offsets are calibrated so that, with its own degradation ladder, it reproduces this net at the stint length it recommends.

regime.label: median of 6 donors, temperature-corrected
regime.derivation: race/practice degradation ratio, stint-fixed-effects estimator on both sessions; each donor's log ratio corrected by the thermal sensitivity (+0.025/degC) times its race-minus-practice track temperature, residuals pooled with the median: japan-2026 0.73x (dT +2 degC -> 0.70), barcelona-2026 0.70x (dT +2 degC -> 0.66), austria-2026 0.58x (dT +2 degC -> 0.56), belgium-2026 0.32x (dT -5 degC -> 0.37), hungary-2026 0.64x (dT +17 degC -> 0.42), italy-2026 0.81x (dT +2 degC -> 0.78) -> management residual 0.61x (spread 0.29 ln); at australia-2026 practice ran at 34 degC and the race is expected at 35 degC (archive race-day mean at Melbourne [2023, 2024]), so 0.61x applies; the old pooled geometric mean would have given 0.61x. australia-2026's own race is never used
